sentence: After twenty years of smoking, he finally managed to give it ___.
explanation: give up = stop/quit (a habit or attempt).

sentence: Could you look ___ my suitcase while I buy the tickets?
explanation: look after = take care of; look for = search; look up = check in a reference.

sentence: If you don't know the word, look it ___ in a dictionary.
explanation: look a word up = find it in a dictionary/reference.

sentence: I'm really looking forward to ___ you again soon.
explanation: look forward TO + -ing: 'to' is a preposition here.

sentence: They put ___ the meeting until everyone could attend.
explanation: put off = postpone.

sentence: I can't put up ___ this noise any longer.
explanation: put up with = tolerate, endure.

sentence: Please carry ___ with your work; don't mind me.
explanation: carry on = continue; carry out = perform (a task).

sentence: The scientists carried ___ a series of experiments.
explanation: carry out = perform, conduct (research, a plan, an order).

sentence: I came ___ an old letter while clearing the attic.
explanation: come across = find/meet by chance.

sentence: She came ___ with a brilliant solution to the problem.
explanation: come up with = produce an idea/plan/solution.

sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

sentence: It took him weeks to get ___ the flu.
explanation: get over an illness/upset = recover from it.

sentence: We're trying to get rid ___ these old boxes.
explanation: get rid OF something = remove it.

sentence: The negotiators refused to give ___ to the hijackers' demands.
explanation: give in (to) = stop arguing and accept; give up = quit.

sentence: She's been going ___ a difficult time at work.
explanation: go through = experience something difficult.

sentence: Hold ___ a moment — I'll check if he's in.
explanation: hold on = wait (especially on the phone).

sentence: The team was let ___ by its own supporters.
explanation: let somebody down = disappoint them by failing to help.

sentence: Police are looking ___ the cause of the crash.
explanation: look into = investigate.

sentence: I can't make ___ what the sign says from here.
explanation: make out = see, hear or understand with difficulty.

sentence: The kids made ___ a story about a stolen dog.
explanation: make up = invent (a story, excuse). Compare make up for = compensate.

sentence: I'll pay you ___ as soon as I get paid.
explanation: pay somebody back = return borrowed money; pay off a debt = finish paying it.

sentence: He picked ___ Spanish surprisingly fast.
explanation: pick up = learn without formal study; also collect (pick somebody up).

sentence: During the tour she pointed ___ the oldest house in town.
explanation: point out = mention/draw attention to a fact.

sentence: Put ___ your coat — it's freezing outside.
explanation: put on = dress in; put off = postpone.

sentence: We've run out ___ coffee again.
explanation: run out OF something = have none left.

sentence: The protesters set ___ at dawn from the village square.
explanation: set off/out = begin a journey; set up = establish.

sentence: They've set ___ a new charity for homeless dogs.
explanation: set up = establish, found (an organization).

sentence: He loves showing ___ his new car to the neighbours.
explanation: show off = try to impress people with your abilities/possessions.

sentence: It took all morning to sort ___ the garage.
explanation: sort out = organize/put in order, or solve (a problem).

sentence: Everyone says she takes ___ her grandmother.
explanation: take after a relative = resemble them in character/looks.

sentence: The plane takes ___ in ten minutes.
explanation: take off = leave the ground (plane); also remove clothes; become successful (career took off).

sentence: Who will take ___ from the current director?
explanation: take over = take control of a job/company.

sentence: She's taken ___ knitting to relax after work.
explanation: take up = start (a hobby, sport, activity).

sentence: I had to turn ___ their invitation because I was ill.
explanation: turn down = reject an offer/invitation; turn up = appear.

sentence: Don't worry — he always turns ___ late.
explanation: turn up = arrive, often unexpectedly or late.

sentence: They worked ___ a compromise after hours of discussion.
explanation: work out = find the solution to; understand; also exercise.

sentence: She was brought ___ by her grandparents.
explanation: bring up a child = raise, educate them.

sentence: The car broke ___ on the motorway.
explanation: break down = stop working (machines/vehicles).

sentence: They broke ___ after only two years of marriage.
explanation: break up = end a relationship.

sentence: The match was called ___ because of the storm.
explanation: call off = cancel an event.

sentence: You go ahead; I'll catch ___ with you later.
explanation: catch up (with) = reach the same point/level as somebody.

sentence: The hotel was full, so we couldn't check ___.
explanation: check in = register; check out = leave and pay.

sentence: She cheered ___ when she heard the news.
explanation: cheer up = become happier (also transitive: cheer somebody up).

sentence: You should cut down ___ sugar if you want to lose weight.
explanation: cut down ON something = reduce it; cut out = eliminate completely.

sentence: The band broke ___ in the middle of the song.
explanation: break off = stop suddenly (speaking, engagement).

sentence: We've decided to do ___ a holiday this year.
explanation: do without = manage without having something.

sentence: Feel free to drop ___ for a coffee any time.
explanation: drop in = pay a casual visit; drop off = fall asleep or deliver.

sentence: I fell ___ with my best friend over a silly remark.
explanation: fall out (with somebody) = have an argument and stop being friendly.

sentence: Please fill ___ this form and sign at the bottom.
explanation: fill in/out a form (British prefers in).

sentence: We found ___ that the flight had been cancelled.
explanation: find out = discover information.

sentence: He stole the pens and got away ___ it.
explanation: get away with something = do wrong without being punished.

sentence: They get ___ on very little money.
explanation: get by = manage to survive (with difficulty).

sentence: The gang gave ___ the stolen paintings to a gallery.
explanation: give away = give free of charge, or reveal (a secret).

sentence: Their son grew ___ and moved abroad.
explanation: grow up = become an adult.

sentence: Hang ___ — this won't take long.
explanation: hang on = wait a moment.

sentence: An accident held ___ the traffic for two hours.
explanation: hold up = delay.

sentence: Hurry ___ or we'll miss the ferry!
explanation: hurry up = do something faster.

sentence: Come on, join ___ — it's easy once you start.
explanation: join in = take part in an activity others are doing.

sentence: It's hard to keep ___ with the latest slang.
explanation: keep up with = stay level with somebody/something changing.

sentence: The old cinema was knocked ___ to build a car park.
explanation: knock down = demolish a building; hit with a vehicle.

sentence: The factory laid ___ two hundred workers.
explanation: lay off = dismiss workers because there is not enough work.

sentence: Don't leave ___ any details in your report.
explanation: leave out = not include, omit.

sentence: The judge let him ___ with a warning.
explanation: let somebody off = not punish them, or give a light punishment.

sentence: The film didn't live up ___ my expectations.
explanation: live up TO something = be as good as expected.

sentence: Looking back ___ it, the risk was worth taking.
explanation: look back ON something = remember and think about the past.

sentence: She looks ___ on people who disagree with her.
explanation: look down on = consider inferior (opposite: look up to).

sentence: The bonus made up ___ all the overtime we had done.
explanation: make up FOR something = compensate for it.

sentence: I've mixed ___ the twins' names again.
explanation: mix up = confuse one thing/person with another.

sentence: They've just moved ___ to their new flat.
explanation: move in = start living in a new home.

sentence: Her grandfather passed ___ last spring.
explanation: pass away = die (a polite expression).

sentence: Several runners passed ___ in the heat.
explanation: pass out = faint.

sentence: Put ___ your toys when you've finished playing.
explanation: put away = put something in its usual place.

sentence: A new proposal was put ___ at the meeting.
explanation: put forward = propose, suggest (an idea, plan, name).

sentence: I ran ___ my old teacher at the airport.
explanation: run into somebody = meet them by chance (also: bump into).

sentence: We saw our guests ___ at the station.
explanation: see somebody off = go with a traveller to say goodbye.

sentence: The concert tickets sold ___ within an hour.
explanation: sell out = all tickets/goods are sold.

sentence: They set ___ to climb the north face in April.
explanation: set out (to do) = begin a job/mission with a goal.

sentence: I stand ___ my decision — it was the right one.
explanation: stand by something = continue to support it; stand by somebody = help and support them.

sentence: What does UNESCO stand ___?
explanation: stand for = represent (letters, initials, principles).

sentence: Her essay stands ___ from the rest of the class.
explanation: stand out = be easy to notice, be better/different.

sentence: Let's start ___ — the first version had too many errors.
explanation: start over = begin again from the beginning.

sentence: To sum ___, we need more time and a bigger budget.
explanation: sum up = summarize the main points.

sentence: They want to try ___ the new software before buying.
explanation: try out = test something to see if it works.

sentence: The caterpillar will turn ___ a butterfly.
explanation: turn into = become, change into.

sentence: Wake ___ — you'll be late for school!
explanation: wake up = stop sleeping.

sentence: These old boots are completely worn ___.
explanation: wear out = become thin/unusable through use.

sentence: The flood wiped ___ the entire harvest.
explanation: wipe out = destroy completely.

sentence: Who is going to deal ___ the angry customer?
explanation: deal with = handle; deal in = trade.

sentence: This old house needs doing ___ before winter.
explanation: do up = repair and decorate a building. (British usage)

sentence: How do you account ___ the sudden change of plan?
explanation: account for = explain the cause of.

sentence: The new manager wants to back ___ the sales team's proposal.
explanation: back up = support (a person, plan); also make a copy of data.

sentence: The fire blew ___ the gas cylinder exploded.
explanation: blow up = explode, or make something explode.

sentence: The store decided to branch ___ into online sales.
explanation: branch out = start doing something new and different.

sentence: The strike brought ___ major changes in the law.
explanation: bring about = cause to happen.

sentence: The scandal brought ___ the government.
explanation: bring down = cause a government/person to lose power; reduce (prices).

sentence: I bumped ___ my neighbour at the dentist's.
explanation: bump into somebody = meet by chance.

sentence: This job calls ___ someone with patience.
explanation: call for = require, demand (circumstances call for action).

sentence: Calm ___ — everything is under control.
explanation: calm down = become less angry/upset.

sentence: Do come round ___ dinner next week.
explanation: come round = visit; come round FOR dinner/TO our place.

sentence: You can count ___ me if you need help.
explanation: count on somebody = rely on them.

sentence: The subject cropped ___ again at dinner.
explanation: crop up = appear or happen unexpectedly.

sentence: Our street was cut ___ for three hours after the storm.
explanation: cut off = disconnected (power, phone); isolate (a village cut off by snow).

sentence: Lawyers are drawing ___ the contract now.
explanation: draw up = prepare and write (a contract, list, plan).

sentence: The plane will drop ___ the parcels at the next farm.
explanation: drop off = deliver somebody/something; also become less (sales dropped off).

sentence: He ended ___ selling insurance, though he'd trained as a chef.
explanation: end up = finally be in a place/situation/state.

sentence: It's time you faced up ___ your responsibilities.
explanation: face up TO something = accept and deal with something difficult.

sentence: The deal fell ___ at the last minute.
explanation: fall through = (a plan/deal) fail to happen.

sentence: I can't figure ___ how this app works.
explanation: figure out = understand after thinking.

sentence: A sales rep will follow ___ your enquiry next week.
explanation: follow up = take further action after something.

sentence: The players are gearing ___ for the final.
explanation: gear up for = prepare for a big event.

sentence: Please hand ___ your essays by Friday.
hint: give to a person in authority
explanation: hand in = give work/documents to somebody in authority.

sentence: The two founders hit it ___ immediately.
explanation: hit it off = like each other and become friendly quickly.

sentence: We need to iron ___ a few details before signing.
explanation: iron out = remove small problems/differences.

sentence: She keyed ___ the password and logged on.
explanation: key in = type in (a password, code).

sentence: The match kicks ___ at three o'clock.
explanation: kick off = (of a match) start.

sentence: Prices levelled ___ after the crazy spring market.
explanation: level off = stop rising or falling and stay the same.

sentence: They live ___ their pension and a small rent.
explanation: live off = have as income/food; live on = have as income (money).

sentence: It's wise to look ___ before making a career move.
explanation: look ahead = think about and plan for the future.

sentence: The new stadium made ___ an impressive sight.
explanation: make for = produce a particular result (make for a good atmosphere); also move towards.

sentence: Can we narrow the list ___ to three names?
explanation: narrow down = reduce the number of possibilities.

sentence: Many consumers now opt ___ cheaper brands.
explanation: opt for something = choose it.

sentence: The old buses are being phased ___ next year.
explanation: phase out = stop using something gradually.

sentence: The ministry tried to play ___ the incident.
explanation: play down = make something seem less important (opposite: play up).

sentence: The doctors pulled him ___ after a difficult night.
explanation: pull through = recover from a serious illness.

sentence: She put her ideas ___ clearly and confidently.
explanation: put across = communicate an idea successfully.

sentence: He puts his success down ___ hard work and a bit of luck.
explanation: put something down TO something = believe it has that cause.

sentence: It's hard to reason ___ someone in a panic.
explanation: reason with somebody = try to persuade them logically.

sentence: Sales figures have tailed ___ since the summer.
explanation: tail off = gradually become less.

sentence: Don't ___ up all the milk — we need some for breakfast.
explanation: use up = finish the whole supply of something.

sentence: The evidence finally backed ___ his version of events.
explanation: back up = support with evidence (a claim backs up a story).

sentence: Can I ___ on these boots before buying them?
explanation: try on = put on clothes/shoes to check the fit.

sentence: The new law will phase ___ disposable plastics by 2030.
explanation: phase out = gradually stop using something.

sentence: We had to call ___ the order because the kitchen had closed.
explanation: call off = cancel.

sentence: She always gets round ___ washing up by promising to do it later.
explanation: get round to = finally find time for; here: avoid a duty — test the preposition after get round.

sentence: The company was ___ up by a larger rival last year.
explanation: 'Take over/take up a company' — here 'was taken up' = absorbed by a bigger firm.

sentence: Please could you look ___ my plants while I'm away?
explanation: 'Look after' = take care of.

sentence: She ___ down an offer from a rival university.
explanation: 'Turn down an offer' = refuse it.

sentence: The meeting has been ___ off until Thursday.
explanation: 'Put off' = postpone to a later time.

sentence: He ___ up the word in an online dictionary.
explanation: 'Look a word up' = check its meaning.

sentence: The rebels finally ___ down the government.
explanation: 'Bring down a government' = cause its collapse.

sentence: He decided to go ___ for the chess championship.
explanation: 'Go in for' = take part in a competition.

sentence: The car ___ down on the motorway and had to be towed.
explanation: 'Break down' = stop functioning (vehicle or machine).

sentence: They're ___ up a new office in the old warehouse district.
explanation: 'Set up' = create or establish.

sentence: The ink ___ off after the first wash.
explanation: 'Come off' = become removed, especially by washing.

sentence: We've ___ out of milk — could you get some more?
explanation: 'Run out of' = exhaust the supply.

sentence: The evening ___ off with a quiz and ended with dancing.
explanation: 'Kick off' = start, informally.
